title: finding(core): `savedViewLimit` admits a saved view's `pagination.pageSize` on `typeof === 'number'` alone — the LOWERING layer under every repaired renderer has no positivity check of its own
body:
`packages/core/src/data-scope/element-data-source.ts`, seat-verified at source on `origin/main` (control: `limit` occurs on **10** lines in the same file, same command):

```ts
:190  function savedViewLimit(view: ElementSavedView | null | undefined): number | undefined {
:191    if (!view) return undefined;
:192    const pagination = view.pagination;
:193    if (isPlainObject(pagination) && typeof pagination.pageSize === 'number') {
:194      return pagination.pageSize;
…
:257  const limit = config.limit ?? savedViewLimit(view);
:258  if (limit !== undefined) composed.limit = limit;
```

⇒ `typeof … === 'number'` admits **0**, **negatives** and **fractions**, and they lower unchecked into the composed `limit` that `ElementDataSourceMapping` feeds back into a node.

## ⭐ Why this one is different from its five siblings

objectui#9853 (`ObjectGrid`, landed), objectui#9897 (`ListView`, landed) and objectui#9925 (`object-kanban` / `object-timeline` / `record:line_items`) are **read points** — each spends a value it was handed.

⭐ **This is the LOWERING layer they all sit under.** It is where a saved view's `pagination.pageSize` becomes a node's `limit`, and it applies **no** positivity check before doing so.

⇒ ⚠️ that does ⛔ **not** make it the single place to fix everything. objectui#9899 measured the decisive counter-fact: the same bad `$top` comes out of the same block **with no `dataSource` binding at all**, where this layer is **never involved**. ⇒ ⭐ **repairing here closes one of two entrances; the read-point resolvers close both.** This card is the second entrance, ⛔ not a replacement for the first.

## ⚠️ What this card must settle FIRST — and it is not 「add a check」

The spec declares the destination positive (`packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts:234`, `limit: z.number().int().positive().optional()`). But the **precedence** question is live and was measured on objectui#9899:

> the gate decides 「did the component author its own cap?」 **by presence alone**, so a component carrying a refused `pagination.pageSize` of 0 counts as having authored one and the bound view's legitimate cap is **never written**. Measured: component `0` + view `7` yields **0, not 7**.

⇒ ⭐ if this layer starts **dropping** a refused view limit, the node falls to its own default — which may be **right**, or may silently override an author's named view. ⚠️ **Drop, clamp and refuse are three different answers here** and the read-point resolvers' answer (fail-soft to the site's own default, one loud diagnostic) was chosen for a **renderer**, ⛔ not for a lowering layer.

⚠️ ⭐ The population is **UNMEASURED**: nobody has counted saved views carrying a non-positive `pagination.pageSize`.

## Dedupe words

- `savedViewLimit pageSize zero`
- `element-data-source limit non-positive`
- `saved view pagination.pageSize lowered to limit`
- `typeof pageSize number admits zero`
- `element data source row cap zero`
